cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the space between people is being tended now.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Pick a bond you care about and hold it steady this week the way a builder holds a stone — no fixing, no steering, no hurry. Just don't drop it.
cells.core:
You can sit with what's between people and not force it into a shape. Where you tend the connection, you let things stay as they are, and because nothing is being pushed, the people in it get to move on their own. Feeling can rise and you don't have to do anything with it; it doesn't need managing from you.

Choose a bond this week and hold it the way a builder holds a stone — steady, no pressure, nothing corrected. That is the work, for now. Some of what you hold won't change, and you'll want to move it. Let it alone. What you're holding will show you what holding without forcing actually does, and you'll keep the answer.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold the space without forcing it closed.

cells.tense: The next mood of the room is being watched for, and you have already started writing it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Look at a bond you've been bracing for. Find a piece of it that's already over — a way of talking, an old arrangement — and set that piece down. Keep the rest. No deadline; do it when you can.
cells.core:
Where you tend what's between people, every exchange is guarded so tightly that nothing is allowed to end. A mood gets caught before it lands, a silence gets filled before it settles, and no bond is ever finished — each one stays open for the next version. It feels like care. From the other chair, it reads like nothing gets to be over.

Caring has another half: knowing what's done. Pick a bond you're bracing for. Find a piece of it that's already over — a way of talking, an old arrangement, a story you keep repairing — and set that piece down. Keep the rest. Room opens for what's still alive once the finished part is out of your hands.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping the connection open so nothing has to end.

cells.tense: Where the space between people is tended, the room has gone quiet, and you are standing behind a door that closed.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: Think of someone you've stopped saying things to. Say a plain true thing to them this week — gently, once — and leave your answer to it alone after that.
cells.core:
Where you tend what's between people, nothing is getting across anymore. You keep the peace by not saying the thing, keep the room calm by not arriving in it, and the space stays clean because nothing true is in it. The care underneath is still there. The connection has gone quiet.

Stay longer with a bond. Pick someone you've stopped saying things to, and speak a plain true thing to them this week — gently, once, then leave it. You don't need to fix what they say back. The point is only to speak across the gap and find out what's on the other side of it. Connection returns through a word first, and the feeling follows.

cells.tense: The space between people is being tended now, and you would say you were only going along with it.
cells.act: cut to the logic and act on it
cells.ask: Take a weight you carry for someone in your head. Say what it would look like if you set it down, then set down a piece of it.
cells.core:
You ease people's rooms — choosing the moment to speak, slowing a pace, holding a silence on purpose — and the calm looks like it simply happened. The moves get made without your name on them. You file them under the other person's mood. The people on the other side of it don't.

Go back to seeing clearly. Take a weight you've been carrying for someone else in your head and say what it would look like if you set it down — one clean line, not a plan. Then set down a piece of it. Your hand is already in how the room feels; this only lets you see it there. There is no deadline on it.
cells.sheetLine: The openings are yours, filed under someone else's mood.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's tending is what others lean on — the record gives the capacity, not the report of it, so each cell keeps to what the capacity is doing rather than what it has been given. The reader could reasonably say the openings come from circumstance or the other person, not from a hand in the room; the ask still works if that read is wrong, because it only asks for an act and lets the result be whatever it is.
